claim_rule: A claim is not the source text. Each English semantic rendering below is a linguistic/translation-dependent claim linked to exact Sanskrit source records and remains challengeable.

claims.semantic_rendering: The verse associates the addressee's adhikara with action (karma) and negates such entitlement/claim with respect to fruits/results (phala).
The verse warns against making the fruit/result of action the operative cause or motive-position of action.
The verse also rejects attachment to inaction/non-action.
The verse connects acting with relinquishment of attachment and with an even stance toward success and failure.
The verse explicitly associates samatva/equanimity with yoga.
The verse contrasts action framed around fruits/results unfavorably with buddhi-yoga and directs the addressee toward refuge in buddhi/discernment.
The verse presents buddhi joined with yoga as changing the agent's relation to good and bad results/consequences and directs the addressee to engage in yoga.
The verse characterizes yoga as kaushala in action; the precise semantic range of kaushala is interpretation-dependent and must not be flattened to a single modern meaning without review.

explicit_non_claims: The source batch does not say that outcomes are irrelevant.
The source batch does not by itself authorize every available action.
The source batch does not erase law, role, safety, evidence, consequence monitoring or accountability.
The source batch does not establish one universal interpretation across all traditions.
The source batch does not prove that equanimity means emotional suppression.
The source batch does not permit ASI governance to treat Wisdom as source truth.
